question: The distributions of electrons in the K, L, and M shell of the chlorine atom are:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The distributions of electrons in the **K, L, and M shells** of the chlorine atom are 2, 8, and 7 respectively.
 
• The chlorine atom has an atomic number of **17**, which determines the number of electrons present in a neutral atom.
 
• Electrons are distributed across shells based on the **2n² rule**, where "n" represents the shell number.
 
• The K shell (n=1) can hold up to 2 electrons, the L shell (n=2) can hold up to 8 electrons, and the M shell (n=3) can hold up to 18 electrons. However, chlorine only needs 7 electrons in the M shell to complete its configuration.
 
• Thus, the electron configuration for chlorine is **2, 8, 7**, aligning with option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron Shell Distribution:**

 
 
• Electrons are arranged in shells around the nucleus of an atom. The shells are labeled as K, L, M, N, etc., starting from the innermost shell.
 
• The capacity of each shell is determined by the formula **2n²**, where "n" represents the shell number.
 
• For chlorine, the atomic number 17 means it has 17 electrons distributed as 2 in K shell, 8 in L shell, and 7 in M shell.
 
 
 
• **Valence Electrons:**
 
 
• Chlorine has **7 valence electrons** in its outermost shell (M shell).
 
• Valence electrons determine an atom's chemical properties, including its ability to bond with other atoms.
 
• Chlorine is highly reactive due to its tendency to gain 1 electron to complete its octet.
 
 
 
• **Chlorine Atom:**
 
 
• Chlorine is a chemical element with the symbol **Cl** and atomic number **17**.
 
• It is a halogen and belongs to Group 17 of the periodic table.
 
• Chlorine is widely used in industry for **water purification, chemical synthesis, and disinfection**.
 
 
 
• **Electronic Configuration:**
 
 
• The electronic configuration of chlorine is **1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵**, representing the distribution of electrons in its orbitals.
 
• This configuration highlights chlorine's tendency to form ionic bonds by gaining an electron, resulting in a stable chloride ion (Cl⁻).
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Context:**
 
 
• Chlorine belongs to the **halogen family**, which includes elements like fluorine, bromine, iodine, and astatine.
 
• Halogens are known for their high reactivity due to their need to gain one electron to complete their octet.
 
• Chlorine's position in the periodic table helps predict its chemical behavior and interactions.
